national_indicator_definition: The indicator presents victims of trafficking in human beings in Bosnia and Herzegovina by sex. Its coverage is based on the definition of trafficking in human beings set out in Article 2 of Directive 2011/36/EU. A registered victim may be a person formally identified as a victim by the competent authority, or a person who meets the criteria of the Directive but has not been formally identified or has declined formal or legal identification.
national_rationale: Trafficking in human beings is a serious violation of human rights and a severe form of crime. Monitoring registered victims by sex provides insight into the composition of identified victims and contributes to monitoring measures to prevent trafficking, protect victims and strengthen institutions. The indicator contributes to monitoring Sustainable Development Goal 16, which concerns peace, justice and strong institutions.
national_methodology_characteristics: The indicator refers to victims of trafficking in human beings as defined in Article 2 of Directive 2011/36/EU. The coverage includes formally identified victims, as well as persons who meet the criteria of the Directive but have not been formally identified or have refused formal or legal identification. The reference period is the calendar year, and data for Bosnia and Herzegovina are presented as absolute numbers, according to values ​​taken from the Eurostat database that consolidates data submitted by countries. The source of data is the Ministry of Security of Bosnia and Herzegovina.
national_long_objective: No specific numerical target has been established for Bosnia and Herzegovina for this indicator under the methodology used for monitoring.
eu_indicator_definition: The indicator presents the number of victims of trafficking in human beings by sex in European Union Member States. Its coverage is based on the definition of trafficking in human beings set out in Article 2 of Directive 2011/36/EU. A registered victim may be a person formally identified as a victim by the competent authority, or a person who meets the criteria of the Directive but has not been formally identified or has declined formal or legal identification.
eu_rationale: Trafficking in human beings is a serious violation of human rights and a severe form of crime. The indicator contributes to monitoring Sustainable Development Goal 16, which concerns peace, justice and strong institutions, and enables monitoring of recorded victims and differences by sex. The data can help assess the scale of recorded cases and support the development of measures for prevention, victim protection and combating trafficking in human beings.
eu_methodology_characteristics: The indicator covers victims of trafficking in human beings as defined in Article 2 of Directive 2011/36/EU. Registered victims include formally identified persons as well as persons who meet the criteria of the Directive but have not been formally identified or have declined formal or legal identification. The reference period is the calendar year, and the unit of measure is the number of victims per 100,000 inhabitants. The data source is the European Statistical System (ESS), with Eurostat compiling data reported by countries.
eu_long_objective: No specific numerical target has been established at European Union level for this indicator under the methodology used for monitoring.
